decision: kept as an exactness repair: four incorrectly empty affine lens configurations recover their exact nonempty geometry, area and classification witnesses

resource_review.correctness_tradeoff: Four retained-chart construction rows previously returned empty regions, losing all area and boundary evidence; all now retain one correct loop. Their first/warm/cloned queries account for the other twelve corrected rows. Correct classification and retained geometry require substantially more query work and memory than the former empty-result path. These costs are accepted under exactness before performance and memory, without a uniform speedup claim.
resource_review.example: For the positive 1e308 translation, construction changes from 426.6 to 393.5 microseconds per region, while the first query changes from an incorrect empty-region lookup at 20.2 ns to a correct result at 119.2 microseconds. Per 64 constructed fixtures retained bytes increase from 918984 to 1686528; first-query retained bytes increase from 64 to 698944. All samples are retained.
resource_review.binary_tradeoff: Timing/allocation ELF files grow by 536/544 bytes; text grows by 640 bytes in both, while rodata shrinks by 64/48 bytes.

next_step: Admit only the guard and its two test modules after staged source-hash verification. Investigate the separately recorded contact-index range-rounding hypothesis after current validation and measurement are terminal; no change for that hypothesis is included here.
limitations: Focused matched probes use 100 ms CPU conditioning and do not measure cold-start latency or establish a full-application speedup. A cheaper incorrect baseline result is not a valid optimization target. The 28 existing curve ignores, complete workspace/pre-push matrix, full floating-point error proof and broader native-prototype admission remain open.
